sections.title: Executive Summary + Investment Thesis
sections.body:
**Executive Summary**
ITC Limited has undergone a significant transformation with the demerger of its Hotels Business into ITC Hotels Limited (ITCHL) effective January 1, 2025. ITCHL, with a 39.88% shareholding by ITC Limited, operates a diverse portfolio of 140+ properties and over 13,000 rooms across six distinctive brands. The company's financial reporting is guided by Indian Accounting Standards (Ind AS), ensuring transparency and consistency in its consolidated financial statements. ITC Limited's financial framework recognizes revenue from the sale of goods and services when control is transferred to the customer, and it accounts for government grants when there is reasonable assurance of compliance with conditions.

**Investment Thesis**
Our investment thesis for ITC Limited is centered on its diversified business portfolio and strategic restructuring efforts, such as the demerger of its Hotels Business. With ITCHL poised for growth as one of the fastest-growing hospitality chains in the country, we believe ITC Limited is well-positioned to capitalize on emerging opportunities in the hospitality sector. However, without specific financial data on revenue, net profit, or net worth, our analysis is limited to understanding the company's financial reporting framework and business structure. Further research is required to assess the company's financial performance and compare it with industry peers, which is not possible based on the provided excerpts.

sections.body:

The company's accounting policies indicate that provisions are recognised when there is a legal or constructive obligation, and it is probable that an outflow of resources will be required to settle the obligation. Additionally, the company's revenue recognition policy is based on the transaction price that the company receives or expects to receive as consideration for goods supplied and services rendered, which may be subject to estimates of variable consideration such as discounts to customers.

The company's financial liabilities, including borrowings and trade payables, are initially recognised at fair value and subsequently measured at amortised cost. sections.title: Recent Developments
sections.body:
Recent Developments: 
The company has reported its financial performance for the year under review, with key highlights including capital expenditure of ₹18.42 billion and depreciation and amortization of ₹16.69 billion. The FMCG segment, which includes cigarettes and other branded packaged foods businesses, accounted for a significant portion of the company's capital expenditure, with ₹8.36 billion spent in the current year. The Agri Business segment reported capital expenditure of ₹1.04 billion, while the Paperboards, Paper and Packaging segment spent ₹3.82 billion. Geographically, the company generated revenue of ₹65,635.22 crore from within India, with no specific figures disclosed for revenue from outside India.

In terms of subsidiary performance, ITC Infotech India Limited reported revenue from operations of ₹3,204.32 crore and a net profit of ₹466.62 crore for the year under review. The company paid a total dividend of ₹488.32 crore, equivalent to ₹53.75 per equity share. Other subsidiaries, including ITC Infotech Limited, UK, and ITC Infotech (USA), Inc., also reported their financial performance, with revenue and net profit figures disclosed in their respective local currencies. Additionally, ITC Infotech India Limited has expanded its global presence by setting up subsidiary companies in several countries, including Brazil, Mexico, France, Germany, Italy, Malaysia, and Saudi Arabia.

sections.title: Bull vs Bear vs Base Case
sections.body:
The 'Bull vs Bear vs Base Case' scenario for ITC Limited is shaped by the company's diversified business portfolio and recent strategic developments. The bull case is supported by ITC's strong performance in its FMCG segment, with revenue from external customers within India standing at ₹65,635.22 crore in 2025, up from ₹60,333.03 crore in 2024. Additionally, the company's decision to demerge its Hotels Business, which posted a profit before exceptional items and tax of ₹572.52 crore for the 9 months ended December 2024, could unlock value for shareholders. The bear case, on the other hand, is concerned with the significant non-cash expenditures and depreciation costs across segments, such as ₹172.84 crore in non-cash expenditure for the FMCG segment in 2025. 

The base case scenario assumes that ITC will continue to leverage its core competencies to drive growth across its business groups, with a focus on effective management of multiple businesses. With capital expenditure of ₹1,327.65 crore in 2025, the company is investing in its future growth. The base case also considers the impact of the demerger of the Hotels Business, which resulted in an exceptional gain of ₹15,163.06 crore in 2025. Given the lack of information on peer comparison, it is challenging to assess ITC's performance relative to its industry counterparts. Overall, the base case scenario anticipates steady growth for ITC, driven by its diversified portfolio and strategic initiatives, with a focus on managing costs and driving operational efficiencies.

Principles of Consolidation The Group’s interests in its subsidiaries, associates and joint ventures are reflected in the Consolidated Financial Statements (CFS) in accordance with the relevant Indian Accounting Standards (Ind AS) specified under Section 133 of the Companies Act, 2013. Subsidiaries (Ind AS 110) Line by line consolidation of the Statement of Profit and Loss and Balance Sheet is done by aggregating like items of assets, liabilities, income and expenses. The excess / deficit of the cost to ITC Limited of its investments in its subsidiaries over its share of net worth (residual interest in the assets of the subsidiaries after deducting all its liabilities) of the subsidiaries at the date of investment in the subsidiaries are treated as goodwill / capital reserve in the CFS. The goodwill is disclosed as an asset and capital reserve as a reserve in the Consolidated Balance Sheet. Profit or loss and each component of other comprehensive income are attributed to the Group as owners and to the non-controlling interest; likewise the non-controlling interests in the net assets of the consolidated subsidiaries is identified and presented separately within Equity in the Consolidated Balance Sheet. Inter-Company transactions within the Group (both Balance Sheet and Profit or loss items) are eliminated for arriving at the Group CFS. CFS is prepared applying uniform accounting policies of ITC Limited to the Group companies. Associates and Joint Ventures (Ind AS 28) An investment in associate and joint venture is initially recognised at cost on the date of the investment, and is inclusive of any goodwill / capital reserve embedded in the cost. Only share of net profits / losses and other comprehensive income of associates / joint ventures is considered in Consolidated Statement of Profit and Loss. The carrying amount of the investment in associates / joint ventures is adjusted by the share of net profits / losses and other comprehensive income in the Consolidated Balance Sheet. 224 REPORT AND ACCOUNTS 2025 ITC Limited
